topic: your first animation is supposed to be bad
audience: Aspiring 2D animators, digital artists, storytime YouTube fans
angle: Self-compassion in creative growth: your first attempt is supposed to fail
hook: Your first animation is supposed to be bad.

slides.headline: Your first animation is supposed to be bad.
slides.subhead: Read this before opening your project today.

slides.headline: The Expectation:
slides.body_text:
You watched 40 hours of master animators on YouTube and thought:

'How hard can a simple walk cycle really be?'

slides.headline: The Reality:
slides.body_text:
Your character's legs are folding backwards.

The arms are detaching from the torso. It looks like a malfunctioning robot tumbling downhill.

slides.headline: The Urge to Rage-Quit:
slides.subhead: You want to delete the file, throw away the stylus, and pretend this never happened.

slides.headline: The Revelation:
slides.body_text:
Your taste develops years ahead of your muscle memory.

Being able to see that your animation looks awkward is proof that your artistic eye is already working.

slides.headline: The Golden Rule of Animation:
slides.body_text:
A finished bad animation teaches you 100x more than an unfinished masterpiece.

Embrace the cringe. It's the only toll booth on the road to mastery.
slides.handwritten_note: ✦ save this for your next project

slides.headline: Be honest in the comments:
slides.cta_text:
What was your very first animation or drawing? Share your beginner cringe!
(Tell me I'm not the only one ➔)
